newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close just shy of even.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close just shy of even.

text.p: Argentine stocks recovered virtually all their losses at the close of a choppy session's trading Monday, dealers said.
"The market slipped on profit-taking but then recovered at the close, mirroring action in New York," said dealer Emilio Alessandro of brokers Alessandro.
The weighted MerVal index ended off 0.1 percent at 674.38 against a session low of 670.08 and a high of 678.44.
Traders forecast prices could continue to seesaw Tuesday but the undertone would remain positive, despite a Caspian Securities weightings cut and devaluation pressures in Brazil.

"The market will start to regroup because it's oversold, as Caspian noted today. But because foreign investment flows are strong the bolsa should be able to weather profit-taking," said an analyst at a private bank.
Caspian advised trimming Latin American weightings in Argentine stocks to five percent from eight percent.
Mounting calls for a quicker devaluation of the Real currency in Brazil to fight a yawning trade gap also briefly sent some jitters through the local market, traders said.
"We've grown used to these fears and their effect should be short-lived," said Alessandro.
He said the market was underpinned by an imminent $2.0 billion bond issue whose road show begins later this week.
The bolsa's all-share index closed up 0.3 percent Monday, with losers outpacing winners 29 to 19 and 22 stocks ending flat.
Floor volume picked up to a moderately strong 27 million pesos from 25 million Friday, while over-the-counter deals remained hefty at 167.5 million pesos against 151.6 million Friday.

Heaviest market losers included oil firms Sol Petroleo and Astra, which pulled back 3.2 percent and 2.0 percent in keeping with a downward correction in world crude prices, and construction company Polledo, off 1.9 percent.
Top main-tier performers were Telecom, up 1.4 percent, Siderca and Telefonica, both up 1.1 percent, and carmaker Ciadea, up 1.0 percent.
